summary: 우리나라에서는 미조로, 호소와 소택지, 간척지, 하천, 하구, 해안, 연못, 물가 풀밭 등에서 지낸다. 땅 위에 둥지를 짓고 몸깃과 가슴깃을 바닥에 깔며, 녹색 빛이 도는 담갈색 알을 9~12개 낳는다. 미국과 캐나다 동부에 분포한다.

art.subject: American Black Duck (Anas rubripes), adult male: body very dark blackish brown with fine paler buff fringes; head and neck paler greyish buff, finely streaked dark, with a darker crown and a dark line through the eye, contrasting with the dark body; speculum glossy violet-blue, bordered black, with at most a thin white line along its rear edge and no white bar in front; white underwing coverts, conspicuous in flight. Unmarked yellow to greenish-yellow bill; dark eye; orange-red legs and feet.
art.pose: swimming at the edge of a pond, side view
art.scene: Korean coastal wetland: a pond and grassy waterside near an estuary; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view swimming: blackish-brown body, paler greyish-buff streaked head and neck with a dark crown and eye-stripe, unmarked greenish-yellow bill, no white on the tertials
adult, wing detail spread from above: violet-blue speculum bordered black, only a thin white line along the rear edge of the secondaries, no white bar in front of the speculum
art.build: Large dabbling duck, 48–56cm, the size and shape of a Mallard; heavy body, rounded head and medium neck. Bill flat and broad, about as long as the head. Legs orange-red, set midway under the body. In flight the very dark body and upperwing contrast sharply with the bright white underwing. Female like the male, but the bill dull olive-green with dark mottling and the legs duller orange-brown.
avoid: Do not give it a black bill with a yellow tip, a dark cheek stripe or white tertials; those mark the Eastern Spot-billed Duck (Anas zonorhyncha).
Do not paint white bars on both sides of the speculum or a pale mottled brown body (female Mallard).
Do not paint a green head; males have no bright breeding colours like a Mallard drake.
